page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.4 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on external storage options, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. In memory operations, it registers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2132.58 GB/sec, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. Cryptographic and compression tasks are supported by hardware instruction sets, yielding a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 25.14 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 161.64 GB/sec.

Given its high core count and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, where it scores 28295.0 on Geekbench, and static web serving, which reaches a throughput of 23.2 GB/sec. Additionally, it can handle moderate database operations and light language model inference, processing 57.07 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B parameter model. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for large-scale deep learning training or high-IOPS storage-heavy databases.
